findings.title: `queued` default is set once at import time, not per instance.
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` runs once, when the class is defined. Every `AssignmentSource` built afterwards, including each one from `from_integration`, gets the same timestamp: the moment the worker process started. Any use of `queued` (ordering, staleness checks, debugging) will be wrong. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

held.title: Task kwargs now carry a raw `datetime`, which a JSON task serializer cannot encode.
held.body: `assignment_source.to_dict()` uses `asdict`, so `queued` stays a `datetime` object inside the `apply_async` kwargs. If the task queue serializes kwargs as JSON (or is moved to JSON later), enqueueing fails for every assignment that starts from an integration webhook, and the inbound assignment errors after the DB write. I could not see which serializer this task uses. To be safe, write `queued` as an ISO string in `to_dict` and parse it back in `from_dict`.
